bw: Excess water dilutes the blood sodium
Sweating, vomiting or diuretics can cause it
tp: Causes also include sweating, vomiting, diarrhea, diuretics, diabetes and acidosis.

ww.Hypernatremia: Hypernatremia is an abnormally high blood sodium.
ww.Hypokalemia: Hypokalemia is a low blood potassium.

evidence: Hyponatremia is a lower-than-normal concentration of sodium, usually associated with excess water accumulation in the body, which dilutes the sodium.

bw: Heart will not relax and may stop within minutes
tp: It can also cause confusion, numbness and weakened respiratory muscles through partial depolarization of cell membranes.

ww.Hypokalemia: Low potassium hyperpolarizes neuron membranes and reduces their responses.
ww.Hypercalcemia: The seizing, non-relaxing heart is the described effect of high potassium.

evidence: Hyperkalemia, an elevated potassium blood level, also can impair the function of skeletal muscles, the nervous system, and the heart.

tp: The kidneys usually conserve phosphate when it is depleted, but this fails during starvation.
evidence: Hypophosphatemia, or abnormally low phosphate blood levels, occurs with heavy use of antacids, during alcohol withdrawal, and during malnourishment.

bw: Cell destruction dumps it into the ECF
tp: Phosphate is a major constituent of the ICF and of nucleic acids, so cell breakdown raises blood levels.

ww.Hyperkalemia: Hyperkalemia is high potassium, though cell destruction raises that too.

evidence: Hyperphosphatemia, or abnormally increased levels of phosphates in the blood, occurs if there is decreased renal function or in cases of acute lymphocytic leukemia.
